Looping in a couple suggestions from pricing/legal standpoint. Lauren, thanks for the clear framing — here is language I'd propose in Exhibit B to resolve both sides:

Proposed clause (redline text):
"Binding Price Matrix" means the table set forth in Exhibit B that establishes the Contractual Floor and Contractual Ceiling for each monthly billing period. The Contractual Floor shall be the minimum billable usage for which Customer will be invoiced. The Contractual Ceiling shall be the maximum billable amount for which Redwood may invoice in a given monthly billing period, subject to the True-Up Procedure.

True-Up Procedure: Billing in excess of the Contractual Ceiling during the Initial 90-Day Ramp period shall be subject to a discretionary smoothing credit at Redwood's sole discretion. Thereafter, billing deviations will be reconciled via monthly true-up with a 30-day settlement window unless Customer elects a quarterly true-up in writing.

Negotiation levers:
- If Boreal wants no hard cap, offer soft bands + 30-day true-up and a 10% smoothing buffer for first two quarters.
- If Boreal insists on hard ceilings, we ask for a 12-month minimum commitment at the middle tier (reduces our downside).

Marissa: please confirm the floor/ceiling numbers in the attached spreadsheet that can be inserted into Exhibit B if we land on hard caps.

-Karthik
